sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a step change rather than a smooth compound: growth ran 46.2% in FY2017 and 49.1% in FY2020, then slowed to 8.9% in FY2025 [D41][D194][D446].
The FY2020 step came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the EU in the third quarter of 2020 [P51].
FY2024 broke the trend with an operating loss of $233 million, as $4.6 billion of AIPR&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine, hit operating expenses [F24][P11].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO is the franchise: it was 85.9% of FY2025 revenue and added 0.7pp of the 8.9% growth [D529][D531][D446].
In FY2025 the growth engine shifted to ALYFTREK, which contributed 7.6pp on $838 million of sales, and to the U.S., which added 7.8pp [D590][S69][D482].
Net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, in 2025 on continued demand, while Europe grew only 0.2% [P3][D495].
Operating costs fell 30.4% while revenue grew 8.9%, so revenue growth exceeded operating-cost growth by 39.3pp, at 8.9% revenue growth [D457][D446][D464].
Diluted EPS rose to $15.32 from $13.89 in FY2023 while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million, so per-share growth tracked net income [F75][F73][X137][D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [F35][D663][D662].
The 36.9pp margin recovery in FY2025 came mostly from the 37.7pp swing in other lines as the prior-year AIPR&D charge did not repeat, with SG&A a 1.3pp drag [D452][D468][D467].
Cost of sales held at 13.8% of revenue in 2025 as a lower overall royalty rate for the CF medicines offset other costs [P4][D425].
In FY2025 net margin of 32.9% sat 1.8pp below the 34.8% operating margin, a gap the pack puts at -1.8pp [F55][F35][D708].
Operating cash flow of $3.63 billion was 0.92x net income in FY2025, below the 1.16x window median, and free cash flow was 0.81x [F85][F45][D434][D698][D435].
Operating cash flow was primarily due to income from operations of $4.2 billion [P1][F25].
Free cash flow margin was 26.6%, below the 32.8% window median, as capex rose 47.0% to $438 million, 2.09x D&A [D431][D669][D447][F95][D436].
Stock-based compensation was 18.9% of operating cash flow, and inventory days reached 373, up 85 days [D437][D444][D397].
Net cash was $12.3 billion, 102.7% of revenue, against a -50.7% peer median and in the 88th percentile of eight peers [D439][D440][D692][D691].
Cash and investments rose to $12.3 billion from $11.2 billion primarily due to increased cash and marketable securities from product revenue [D438][D392][P2].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion absorbed 63.2% of free cash flow in FY2025, yet the diluted share count was unchanged at 258.0 million [D441][D442][X137][D459].
The current ratio of 2.90x sits below the 3.52x window median, with working capital of $7.34 billion [F185][D678][F175].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 in FY2025, the third straight year of increase from 214 in FY2023 [D444][D397][D350].
Inventory is building far faster than the 8.9% revenue growth, which ties up cash and raises the risk of write-downs if demand shifts [D446].
The effective tax rate fell 300.7pp to 14.9% from 315.5% in FY2024 [D433][D390].
The FY2024 rate reflected $4.4 billion of non-deductible AIPR&D from Alpine, so the FY2025 rate is the normalised level rather than a new benefit [P5].
The tax swing is a base effect, not a red flag, and the FY2019 buyback restatement of $192.0 million is immaterial to the trend [X141].
If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays at or below the FY2025 0.7% in the FY2026 10-K, the franchise has plateaued [D530].
If days inventory outstanding rises above the FY2025 373 days in the FY2026 10-K, the inventory build is worsening [D444].
If the operating margin falls below the 31.8% window median in the FY2026 10-K, the FY2025 recovery has reversed [D663].
